problem: Path-ranking VLN models (VLN-BERT, AirBert) reach high R2R success, but it is unknown which instruction tokens they actually use. Prior diagnostic work only covered sequential agents, so path-ranking models were never examined.
motivation: Spatial and directional words (left/right, turn around) are what distinguish navigation from other vision-language tasks, yet a large gap to human performance remains. The authors probe with token-masking and counterfactual swaps to see whether path-ranking models exploit shortcuts rather than real spatial grounding.
key_idea: Mask or swap token classes (nouns, verbs, spatial, left/right) in R2R instructions at test time to show that path-ranking VLN models rely almost only on nouns, then mitigate this with path-shuffling hard negatives and a spatial-token masked-language-modeling loss.
insight: Path-ranking models drop about 12-16 SR points only when nouns are masked. Masking or swapping left/right barely changes them (VLN-BERT swap: 55.90 to 56.07), whereas the sequential Rec-VLN-BERT drops under every masking (swap: 62.75 to 46.70). The authors attribute this to path-ranking seeing the whole path, which allows noun pattern-matching. Shuffling + SLL raises SR and makes the model sensitive to swap (-3.19), whereas adding programmatically generated direction-dense instructions changes nothing.
method: Token-masking diagnostic: at test time mask or replace tokens of a class (nouns, adjectives, verbs, objects, numerals, a 13-word spatial list, left/right) and compare SR on R2R val-unseen; models are unchanged.
Swap counterfactual: replace left with right and vice versa, so a model that follows directions should fail.
Unimodal ablations: mask all language or all vision tokens to measure dataset bias and lower bounds.
Shuffling: AirBert-inspired hard negatives made by shuffling the image-token order of the correct path, used in the path-ranking fine-tuning of VLN-BERT.
Spatial Language Loss (SLL): 10 extra epochs at the end of stage 3 where 100% of spatial tokens are masked and only they are predicted (pure MLM), then normal fine-tuning.

Passive data: about 6k rule-generated path-instruction pairs on MP3D training scenes (paths of 5-10 edges), with object-sparse, direction-dense text (e.g. 'Go forward and walk 3 meters. Turn right...'), added to R2R training.
Counterfactual sanity check: 92.87% of turns in val-unseen have at least one alternative path, averaging 1.62 per turn, so direction words do matter.

setting.backbone: VLN-BERT (ViLBERT-based path-ranking, retrained with modifications); analysed also AirBert, Recurrent-VLN-BERT, PREVALENT
setting.training_data: R2R train plus web pretraining (Conceptual Captions etc.) following VLN-BERT; variants add shuffled hard negatives or about 6k generated instruction-path pairs on MP3D training scenes
setting.observation: panoramic RGB image features along candidate paths plus text instruction
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (path ranking over beam-search candidate paths; sequential for Rec-VLN-BERT)
setting.privileged: none (path-ranking models score full candidate paths, which is inherent to the setup)

numbers.extra: path-ranking with beam-search candidates; own retrained VLN-BERT baseline is 55.90 SR

results: Path-ranking models (VLN-BERT, AirBert) lose SR only when nouns are masked (VLN-BERT 55.90 to 43.68) and are almost unaffected by spatial masking or left/right swap. The sequential Rec-VLN-BERT is affected by all masks. Shuffling + SLL improves the retrained VLN-BERT on R2R val-unseen from 55.90 to 60.62 SR and adds swap sensitivity (-3.19). Passive-data training does not help (54.53 SR).
limitations: Diagnosis is limited to R2R, three models, and hand-picked token lists. Only VLN-BERT is used for the training fixes, and their generalisation to AirBert is assumed.

The retrained VLN-BERT baseline was 3.36 SR below the published number (attributed to hardware and driver differences). The generated data comes from a single rule-based generator on MP3D and did not help.
The cause is only hypothesised (path-ranking shortcut, scarce environments), with no controlled test.
